results.content: a supervised cross-lingual word embedding alignment system for English and Hindi using the Procrustes method and CSLS for comparison. This project implements both supervised and unsupervised cross-lingual word embedding alignment methods for aligning English and Hindi word embeddings. 1. Supervised Procrustes Alignment: Uses a bilingual lexicon to learn an orthogonal mapping between English and Hindi embeddings. • Bilingual Lexicon: The MUSE dataset provides a list of English-Hindi word pairs used for supervised alignment. • The Procrustes method is used to learn an orthogonal transformation that maps the English embeddings to the Hindi embeddings. • Unsupervised CSLS + Adversarial Training performs well when no bilingual dictionary is available, but the results are generally less accurate than the supervised method. This project demonstrates the implementation and evaluation of both supervised and unsupervised methods for cross-lingual word embedding alignment. a supervised cross-lingual word embedding alignment system for English and Hindi using the Procrustes method and CSLS for comparison.

In the second set of experiments, we recreate the benchmarks from (Grave et al., 2019), and we show that our method can align word embedding spaces without a good initialization matrix. We have underlined some mathematical properties of the Wasserstein-Procrustes problem and hence used the concept of the different natural initialization transformations in an iterative algorithm to achieve improved results for mapping word embeddings between different languages. We hope that our rethinking of the Wasserstein-Procrustes problem would enable further research and would eventually help develop better algorithms for aligning word embeddings across languages, especially taking into account that most unsupervised approaches try to minimize loss functions different from Objective 2.

results.title: A Novel Unsupervised Approach for Cross-Lingual Word Alignment in Low Isomorphic Embedding Spaces | IEEE Journals & Magazine | IEEE Xplore
results.content: # A Novel Unsupervised Approach for Cross-Lingual Word Alignment in Low Isomorphic Embedding Spaces. Cross-lingual word alignment is the task for word translation between monolingual word embedding spaces of two different languages. Cross-lingual word alignment is the task for word translation between monolingual word embedding spaces of two different languages. The unsupervised adversarial approaches, which utilize generative adversarial networks (GANs) to map the global monolingual space to another space, can eliminate the need for aligned data. In addition, these approaches often fail to account for the low isomorphism between language pairs, which prevents capturing the non-linear relationship contained in cross-lingual embedding spaces. To address these issues, we propose a novel unsupervised unified framework with an adaptive training objective for the GANs' improvement (ATOGAN) and a local mapping (LM) strategy for exploring the non-linear relationship. We present ATOGAN to learn bi-directional global mapping using unaligned word embeddings, which integrates particle swarm optimization (PSO) to adaptively select the training objective for preventing mode collapse and gradient disappearance. Then, we design an LM strategy based on the guidance of dictionaries generated by trained ATOGAN to alleviate reliance on isomorphism assumption for purely linear mapping. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method for cross-lingual word alignment in low isomorphic embedding spaces (distant language pairs). **Published in:** IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing ( Volume: 31). The distributed word embeddings representation learning in context can capture the internal information of language. Cross-lingual word alignment transfers word embeddings of various languages into a common space based on word-distributed representation learning to extend the application of word embeddings to other cross-lingual applications. Through cross-lingual word alignment, we could capture the cross-lingual embeddings of different languages at the word level and use them to induce bilingual lexicons, both of which play an important role in language understanding and generation tasks for various cross-lingual applications, such as machine translation [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], cross-lingual named entity recognition [6], [7], cross-lingual sentiment analysis [8], multi-word term alignments [9] and cross-lingual text classification [10], etc. Generally, an important fact is that the corpus undergoes pre-processing through a word tokenizer before cross-lingual word alignment. # References. **References is not available for this document.**.
